# Ciprofloxacin PO

---

# Usual dose:

250-500 mg q12h

# Dose adjustments for renal or hepatic insufficiency:

# Creatinine clearance (ml/min) Dose adjustment

< 30250 mg q12h

Hemodialysis  250-500 mg q24h

# Drug Interactions:

Hypoglycemia that can lead to coma especially in diabetics taking oral hypoglycemic medicine or insulin.

Calcium, dairy products, iron, zinc, magnesium, aluminum  inhibit the absorption of oral ciprofloxacin.  Give ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after these drugs.

Increases effects of caffeine and theophylline by inhibiting  metabolism.

Monitor the patient for signs of agitation or anxiety.

Increases the effect of warfarin.  Monitor international normalized ratio (INR) ratio (INR) frequently in patients taking warfarin.

# Adverse Drug Reactions:

# FDA Drug Safety Communication

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration advised that the serious side effects associated with fluoroquinolone antibacterial drugs generally outweigh the benefits for patients with acute sinusitis, acute bronchitis, and uncomplicated urinary tract infections who have other treatment options. For patients with these conditions, fluoroquinolones should be reserved for those who do not have alternative treatment options.

An FDA safety review has shown that fluoroquinolones when used systemically are associated with disabling and potentially permanent serious side effects that can occur together. These side effects can involve the tendons, muscles, joints, nerves, and central nervous system.

FDA identified cases of hypoglycemic coma, resulting in death in some instances. Most pateints had risk factors for hypoglycemia such as older age, diabetes, renal insufficiency, and concomitant use of hypoglycemic drugs, especally sulfonylureas.  FDA also identified reports of additional mental health side effects, and requires that all fluoroquinolones include six psychiatric adverse reactions (disturbance in attention, memory impairment, delirium, nervousness, agitation and disorientation).

# Other adverse reactions:

Nausea/vomiting, diarrhea, dizziness, confusion, CNS stimulation, rare seizures, rare QT interval prolongation, and tendinitis/tendon rupture. Six psychiatric adverse reactions including disturbance in attention, memory impairment, delirium, nervousness, agitation and disorientation.

Hypoglycemia that can lead to coma, occuring more frequently in the elderly and those with diabetes.

# Pregnancy Risk Factor Category: C
